'''Carlos Guido Bollini''' (15 January 1926 - 12 October 2009) was a physicist from [[Argentina]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Carlos Guido Bollini {{!}} Fundación Konex |url=https://www.fundacionkonex.org/ |access-date=2025-12-28 |website=www.fundacionkonex.org |language=es}}</ref> He is known for being one of the driving forces behind the development of physics in his country and for developing, together with [[Juan José Giambiagi]], the method of [[dimensional regularization]],<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last=Bollini |first=C. G. |last2=Giambiagi |first2=J. J. |date=1972-11-01 |title=Dimensional renorinalization : The number of dimensions as a regularizing parameter |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02895558 |journal=Il Nuovo Cimento B (1971-1996) |language=en |volume=12 |issue=1 |pages=20–26 |doi=10.1007/BF02895558 |issn=1826-9877|url-access=subscription }}</ref> which is used nowadays in high-energy physics.

== Biography ==
Bollini was born in Lomas de Zamora in 1926.<ref name=":0" /> He went to the industrial high-school Ingeniero Huergo and, afterwards, he continued his studies at the [[Universidad Nacional de La Plata]]. He obtained his degree in physics and, in 1953, he was awarded the title of Doctor en Ciencias Fisicomatemáticas (PhD in mathematical physics). After obtaining his PhD, he worked as teaching assistant at the Facultad de Ciencias Exactas y Naturales de la [[University of Buenos Aires|Universidad de Buenos Aires]]. Subsequently, he lived a few months in [[Bariloche]], where he was a teacher at the [[Balseiro Institute|Instituto Balseiro]].{{Citation needed|date=January 2026}}

Between 1958 and 1960 he was a fellow of the [[National Scientific and Technical Research Council|CONICET]] at the [[Imperial College London|Imperial College of Science and Technology.]]<ref name=":0" /> There, he spent two year working under the supervision of Nobel prize [[Abdus Salam]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-11-01 |title=Periodico el barrio |url=https://periodicoelbarrio.com.ar/ |access-date=2025-12-28 |language=en-US}}</ref>

He came back to the country to become professor at the Physics Department of the Facultad de Ciencias Exactas, [[University of Buenos Aires|Universidad de Buenos Aires]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |title=Pesar por el fallecimiento del físico Carlos Bollini |url=https://www.lanacion.com.ar/1187702-pesar-por-el-fallecimiento-del-fisico-carlos-bollini |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180406040613/https://www.lanacion.com.ar/1187702-pesar-por-el-fallecimiento-del-fisico-carlos-bollini |archive-date=2018-04-06 |access-date=2025-12-28 |language=es}}</ref> In 1969 he was one of the 300 researchers that had to quit their positions at the [[University of Buenos Aires|Universidad de Buenos Aires]] after the [[La Noche de los Bastones Largos|Noche de los Bastones Largos]] (night of the long truncheons). At that time, he moved to the city of La Plata, where he worked at the Physics Department of the [[National University of La Plata|Universidad Nacional de La Plata]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=2014-02-01 |title=Revolutionary physics in reactionary Argentina |url=https://physicstoday.aip.org/features/revolutionary-physics-in-reactionary-argentina |access-date=2026-01-10 |website=PHYSICS TODAY |language=en |doi=10.1063/PT.3.2277}}</ref>

His most cited<ref>{{Cite web |title=INSPIRE |url=https://inspirehep.net/authors/1034870?ui-citation-summary=true |access-date=2025-12-28 |website=inspirehep.net}}</ref> contribution was published in 1972 in collaboration with [[Juan José Giambiagi]].<ref name=":2" /> This work is related to the method of [[dimensional regularization]], a method used in the [[renormalization]] of [[quantum field theories]]. The same idea was developed in parallel<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last='t Hooft |first=G. |last2=Veltman |first2=M. |date=1972-07-01 |title=Regularization and renormalization of gauge fields |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0550321372902799 |journal=Nuclear Physics B |volume=44 |issue=1 |pages=189–213 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(72)90279-9 |issn=0550-3213}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Schaposnik |first=Fidel Arturo |date=2000 |title=Sobre el premio Nobel de física 1999 |journal=Ciencia Hoy |volume=10 |issue=55 |pages=35}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Schaposnik |first=Fidel Arturo |title=Sobre el premio Nobel de física 1999 |url=https://sites.google.com/site/schaposnik/sobreelpremionobeldef%C3%ADsica1999 |access-date=2026-01-12 |website=sites.google.com |language=en-US}}</ref> by a group of Dutch researchers ([[Gerard 't Hooft|Gerardus 't Hooft]] and [[Martinus J. G. Veltman]]). Even though Bollini and Giambagi were the first to submit their work, the manuscript was rejected by Physics Letters B,<ref name=":4" /> so they decided to send it to Il Nuovo Cimento B; in the meanwhile, the manuscript of the Dutch researchers got published in Nuclear Physics B.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Diario El Dia de La Plata www.eldia.com |url=https://www.eldia.com/nota/2012-11-12-dos-argentinos-calculaban-en-4-e-dimensiones-hace-40-anos |access-date=2025-12-28 |website=www.eldia.com |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bietenholz |first=Wolfgang |last2=Prado |first2=Lilian |date=2014-02-01 |title=Revolutionary physics in reactionary Argentina |url=https://physicstoday.aip.org/features/revolutionary-physics-in-reactionary-argentina |access-date=2025-12-28 |website=PHYSICS TODAY |language=en |doi=10.1063/PT.3.2277}}</ref> The Dutch group was later awarded the Nobel Prize in 1999, partially for this publication.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nobel Prize in Physics 1999 |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1999/summary/ |access-date=2025-12-28 |website=NobelPrize.org |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Advanced information, Nobel Prize in Physics 1999 |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1999/advanced-information/ |access-date=2026-01-12 |website=NobelPrize.org |language=en-US}}</ref> The work of Giambiagi and Bollini was not cited in the Royal Swedish Academy of Science's advanced-information article.<ref name=":5" /> However, Veltman admitted to having seen drafts of Giambiagi and Bollini's work and mentioned “the independent work of Bollini and Giambiagi,” in his Nobel lecture.<ref name=":4" />

In 1976 he had to leave Argentina, after a series of events triggered by the military coup d'état.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Lévy-Bollini |first=Susana |title=Heures volées |publisher=Editorial Dunken |year=2006 |isbn=987-02-1723-0 |edition=1}}</ref> First, in October 1976 he received a letter from the military then in charge of the Universidad de La Plata, saying that they no longer needed his services as professor. Second, in November 1976, he received a similar letter from CONICET. Afterwards, in the middle of one night, he and his family were awakened by the strike of a paramilitary force at their house; they were forced to stay in pijamas in the middle of the street, while their house was searched. After these events, he decided to emigrate from Argentina, initially hired by the [[Instituto de Física Teórica]] in São Paulo, Brazil, and afterwards by the [[Centro Brasileiro de Pesquisas Físicas]] in Rio do Janeiro.<ref name=":4" />

He came back to Argentina in 1984, when the Comisión de Investigaciones de la Provincia de Buenos Aires (Research Commission of the Buenos Aires province) offered him the position of researcher. He was also researcher at the [[National Atomic Energy Commission|Comisión Nacional de Energía Atómica]] (National Atomic Energy Commission), where he worked as leader of the Division of Theoretical Physics and of the Theory Group of the Reactor. In addition, he was full Professor at the Instituto de Física de San Carlos de Bariloche ([[Balseiro Institute|Instituto Balseiro]]).{{Citation needed|date=January 2026}}

== Awards and honors ==

* 2003 Platinum [[Konex Award|Konex award]] in physics.<ref name=":0" />
* 1993 [[Konex Award|Konex award]] in physics and astronomy.<ref name=":0" />
* 1987 Bunge y Born award for his track.<ref name=":0" />
* 1987 Richard Gans prize for his track.{{Citation needed|date=January 2026}}
* 1975 Dr. Teófilo Isnardi award by the [[National Academy of Sciences of Argentina]] (Academia Nacional de Ciencias).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Centro Latino Americano de Fisica |url=https://claffisica.org.br/news-item/a-fisica-perde-carlos-bollini}}</ref>
